note: Undefined and partly defined encodings (POL-ILL-01): bits 15..10 of an instruction word take no part in decoding, and the jump DE field value 11 is refused. Every expect value is read from the cited page image and derived by hand; none comes from this core, an assembler or another implementation.

vectors.cite: S3.3.4 Fig 3.3.4, pdf 51; control instructions table, CLRC row, pdf 56; instruction fetch figure, pdf 28
vectors.derivation: POL-ILL-01 (policy): decode uses bits 9..0 of the word only; bits 15..10 are printed as 'Future Use' in every instruction format (Fig 3.3.1-3.3.4, pdf 50-51) and take no part. The word $FC06 is 111111 in bits 15..10 and 0000 000 110 = $006 in bits 9..0. The control table (pdf 56) prints CLRC as 0000 000 110, 4 cycles, 'CLeaR Carry to zero', Not Interruptable, status change C. So the word acts as CLRC: C 1 -> 0, S, Z and OV keep 0, R7 = $1000 + 1 = $1001 (one word fetched), 4 cycles, prev_interruptible 1 -> 0. Bus (pdf 28): one FETCH at cycle 0 from $1000 carrying the whole word $FC06. Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.

vectors.cite: S3.3.1 Fig 3.3.1, pdf 50; register to register table, ADDR row, pdf 53; S3.1.2, pdf 45; instruction fetch figure, pdf 28
vectors.derivation: POL-ILL-01 (policy): decode uses bits 9..0 of the word only; bits 15..10 are printed as 'Future Use' in every instruction format (Fig 3.3.1-3.3.4, pdf 50-51) and take no part. The word $A4CA is 101001 in bits 15..10 and 0011 001 010 = $0CA in bits 9..0. The register table (pdf 53) prints ADDR SSS, DDD as 0011 SSS DDD, 6 cycles, 'ADD contents of registers SSS and DDD. Results to DDD', status S, Z, C, OV. SSS = 001 (R1 = $0101), DDD = 010 (R2 = $0202): $0202 + $0101 = $0303 (pdf 45): no carry out, no overflow, bit 15 = 0, nonzero, so S = Z = OV = C = 0, clearing their initial 1. R2 = $0303, R7 = $1001, 6 cycles; the row has no Not Interruptable note, so prev_interruptible 0 -> 1. Bus (pdf 28): one FETCH at cycle 0 from $1000 carrying $A4CA. Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.

vectors.cite: S3.3.3 Fig 3.3.3 and footnote, pdf 51; control instructions table, NOP row, pdf 56; instruction fetch figure, pdf 28
vectors.derivation: POL-ILL-01 (policy): decode uses bits 9..0 of the word only; bits 15..10 are printed as 'Future Use' in every instruction format (Fig 3.3.1-3.3.4, pdf 50-51) and take no part. The word $FC35 is 111111 in bits 15..10 and 0000 110 101 = $035 in bits 9..0. The control table (pdf 56) prints NOP <n> as 0000 110 10N, 6 cycles, 'No operation.', no status change; the pdf 51 footnote makes 0000 110 1xx (GSWD R4/R5) a NOP, so N = 1 selects nothing. R7 = $1001, 6 cycles, no register other than R7 and no flag changes (all stay 1); the row has no Not Interruptable note, so prev_interruptible 0 -> 1. Bus (pdf 28): one FETCH at cycle 0 from $1000 carrying $FC35. Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.

vectors.cite: S3.3.5 Fig 3.3.5, pdf 52; jump instructions table, pdf 56; instruction fetch figure, pdf 28; C36
vectors.derivation: POL-ILL-01 (policy): the jump group is 0000 000 100 followed by BB AAAAAA DE and AAAAAAAAAA (Fig 3.3.5, pdf 52); bits 0-1 of the second word enable or disable the interrupt system. The jump table (pdf 56) prints DE = 00 (J, JSR), 01 (JE, JSRE) and 10 (JD, JSRD) only, so DE = 11 is an undefined encoding and is refused with the sticky fault UNSUPPORTED_JUMP_DE. DE sits in the second word, so the refusal comes after it is read: FETCH of $0004 at cycle 0 from $1000 (pdf 28), then the READ of the second word $0313 (11 000100 11: BB = 11, DE = 11) at $1001 at cycle 4; the third word is not read. Cycles 4 + 4 = 8 (inference, C36: no jump figure exists; the printed 12 cycles are read as three 4-cycle word transfers). R7 goes back to the offender $1000, run_state becomes FAULTED, and registers, flags, INTFF and prev_interruptible keep their values. Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.

vectors.cite: S3.3.1 Fig 3.3.1, pdf 50; register to register table, MOVR, TSTR and JR rows and footnote, pdf 53; instruction fetch figure, pdf 28
vectors.asm: TSTR R7 (= MOVR R7, R7 = JR R7), bits 15..10 = 111111
vectors.derivation: POL-ILL-01 (policy): decode uses bits 9..0 of the word only; bits 15..10 are printed as 'Future Use' in every instruction format (Fig 3.3.1-3.3.4, pdf 50-51) and take no part. The word $FCBF is 111111 in bits 15..10 and 0010 111 111 = $0BF in bits 9..0. On pdf 53, 0010 111 111 matches MOVR SSS, DDD (SSS = DDD = 111), TSTR SSS (both fields 111) and JR SSS (DDD printed 111). After the fetch R7 = $1001; R7 read as a source is that incremented PC (inference from pdf 28 and POL-STK-01). MOVR R7, R7: R7 = $1001, DDD = 7 so 6 + 1 = 7 cycles; TSTR R7: tests $1001, SSS = 7 so 6 + 1 = 7 cycles; JR R7: jump to $1001, 7 cycles. All three give R7 = $1001, S = 0 and Z = 0 from $1001 (status S, Z, pdf 45), 7 cycles. Init flags 1: S and Z clear, OV and C stay 1; prev_interruptible 0 -> 1 (no Not Interruptable note). Bus (pdf 28): one FETCH at cycle 0 from $1000 carrying $FCBF. Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.
